root.label: Evaluation Order
root.note: C++ separates syntax grouping from runtime sequencing and defines strict rules for side-effect visibility.

children.label: Precedence vs Ordering
children.note: Syntax trees bind operands to operators without dictating which subexpression runs first.

children.label: Precedence builds parse tree
children.note: Higher-precedence operators claim neighboring operands before lower-precedence operators.

children.label: Associativity groups ties
children.note: Left or right associativity resolves equal-precedence chains such as a - b - c.

children.label: Order picks runtime schedule
children.note: The optimizer schedules subexpressions freely unless a sequencing edge constrains them.

children.label: Sequencing Relations
children.note: Every pair of single-thread evaluations is sequenced, indeterminately sequenced, or unsequenced.

children.label: Sequenced before
children.note: Value computation and all side effects of the first complete before the second starts.

children.label: Indeterminately sequenced
children.note: Either evaluation finishes before the other without interleaving instructions.

children.label: Unsequenced conflicts
children.note: Two unsequenced accesses to one scalar where at least one writes cause undefined behavior.

children.label: C++17 Guarantees
children.note: P0145R3 ordered postfix chains, shifts, assignments, and separated function arguments.

children.label: Postfix and subscript left-first
children.note: Member access and array indexing always finish evaluating the left object first.

children.label: Shifts evaluate left-to-right
children.note: Chained stream insertions and bit shifts sequence the left operand before the right.

children.label: Assignment right-before-left
children.note: Simple and compound assignments evaluate the right operand completely before the left.

children.label: Arguments cannot interleave
children.note: Each argument finishes without interleaving, preventing nested smart-pointer leaks.

children.label: Short-Circuit & Lists
children.note: Control-flow operators and braced initializers enforce deterministic left-to-right steps.

children.label: Built-in logical operators
children.note: Built-in && and || sequence left before right and skip the right when already decided.

children.label: Ternary conditional
children.note: The condition and its side effects complete before the single chosen branch evaluates.

children.label: Braced initializer lists
children.note: Clauses inside curly braces always evaluate strictly left-to-right.

children.label: Overload Traps
children.note: User-defined operators alter function-call timing and disable short-circuiting.

children.label: Overloaded && evaluates eagerly
children.note: Custom operator&& is a function call, so both operands evaluate even when the left is false.

children.label: Overloaded ops keep order
children.note: Operator syntax preserves the built-in operand order while function notation does not.
